Keywords: Depends yield session database SQLAlchemy AsyncSession generator teardown
Description: Use a generator dependency that yields a DB session and closes it after the request. FastAPI handles teardown on both success and error via the generator protocol.
When to Use: For every endpoint that needs database access
Code Example:
"from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from typing import Annotated

async def get_db():
    async with AsyncSessionLocal() as session:
        yield session

DbSession = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_db)]

@router.get('/')
async def handler(db: DbSession): ..."
Anti-Pattern: Opening DB sessions directly inside route handlers without teardown guarantees — connections leak on error

Keywords: lifespan asynccontextmanager startup shutdown app state resource pool cleanup
Description: Replace deprecated on_event handlers with the lifespan async context manager on the FastAPI app. Code before yield runs on startup; code after runs on shutdown.
When to Use: Initializing Redis pools DB connection pools ML models or any shared resource at startup
Code Example:
"from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # startup: load ML model or open connections
    ml_models['answer'] = load_model()
    yield
    # shutdown: release resources
    ml_models.clear()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)"
Anti-Pattern: Using deprecated @app.on_event('startup') and @app.on_event('shutdown') decorators — marked as deprecated in FastAPI docs

Keywords: class depends callable __call__ init configurable parameterized state
Description: Use a class with __call__ when a dependency needs constructor parameters. FastAPI calls the instance as a function on each request. Enables reusable parameterized logic.
When to Use: When you need configurable dependencies (e.g. checking different permission levels or page size limits)
Anti-Pattern: Using global state or module-level variables for configurable logic

Keywords: Annotated share reuse DRY type alias dependencies common
Description: Create reusable Annotated type aliases for dependencies shared across many routes. This is the official FastAPI-recommended pattern to avoid repeating Depends() everywhere.
When to Use: When the same dependency appears on many routes and you want clean DRY function signatures
Code Example:
"from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Depends

DbSession = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_db)]
CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_active_user)]

@router.get('/me')
async def read_me(user: CurrentUser, db: DbSession): ...

@router.put('/me')
async def update_me(user: CurrentUser, db: DbSession, body: UserUpdate): ..."
Complexity: Depends(get_current_active_user)] on every route — hard to refactor

Keywords: global dependency router app include_router all routes security blanket
Description: Attach dependencies to an entire router or the whole app at include_router time so they run on every matching request — no need to repeat on each route.
When to Use: For blanket auth checks or rate limiting across all routes in a router or the whole app
Code Example:
"# On a router
router = APIRouter(dependencies=[Depends(verify_token)])

# Or at include time
app.include_router(router, dependencies=[Depends(verify_token)])

# Or globally on the app
app = FastAPI(dependencies=[Depends(verify_token)])"
Anti-Pattern: Adding the same Depends to every individual route decorator — fragile and easy to forget on new routes

Keywords: yield try except finally cleanup resource release error handling
Description: Wrap resource teardown in try/finally inside a yielding dependency to guarantee cleanup even when a route handler raises an exception.
When to Use: When teardown must run regardless of success or error (releasing DB locks committing/rolling back transactions)
Code Example:
"async def get_db():
    db = AsyncSessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
        await db.commit()
    except Exception:
        await db.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        await db.close()"
Anti-Pattern: Using try/except without finally — cleanup skipped on uncaught errors

Keywords: lru_cache cache singleton settings once expensive setup
Description: Wrap resource-heavy setup (loading config creating clients) in @lru_cache so it only runs once across all requests. Works with Pydantic Settings for environment variable loading.
When to Use: For dependencies that must initialize once and be reused (settings objects API clients)
Anti-Pattern: Reading env vars or loading config files on every request inside a dependency — unnecessary I/O per request

Keywords: background tasks dependency inject service pattern
Description: Inject BackgroundTasks into a sub-dependency (not just the route handler directly) so that services can schedule background work without being tightly coupled to the route.
When to Use: When a service layer needs to schedule post-response tasks without the route handler managing it directly
Anti-Pattern: Passing BackgroundTasks through multiple layers of function calls manually
